subject: Pilot KPI slate & ops ownership — Novaworks POC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novaworks.com>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@novaworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot KPI slate & ops ownership — Novaworks POC

Hi Sanjay / Leah —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed lightweight success slate so we can move to a signed pilot Statement of Work: what we think you need to validate, who owns what, and the timeline we recommend. I attached a compact KPI template and the initial test dataset manifest we discussed.

Summary of objectives (what success looks like for Novaworks):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 350 ms for typical user prompt (median expected seq length ~120 tokens).
- Throughput: ability to sustain 50 inference requests/sec with P95 latency SLO intact (burst to 120 RPS tolerated for short periods).
- Cost: amortized cost per token <= $0.0009 (target; we will report modeled vs actual).
- Quality: automated eval F1/ROUGE analog > 0.85 on the baseline test set; manual review pass rate >= 86% on representative samples; hallucination incidents < 1% of responses.
- Availability/ops: 99.5% uptime during business hours, <5% error rate for inference calls.

Evaluation plan and cadence:
1) Week 0 (kickoff): finalize test prompts, dataset slices, and API keys (owner: Novaworks product — Sanjay).
2) Week 1: baseline run on current dataset (owner: Redwood infra — Ben). Deliverable: baseline metrics report (latency, throughput, cost/token, quality metrics).
3) Week 2: model/config iterations (quantization / batching / cache profiles) and rerun. Deliverable: delta report + recommended config. (owner: Redwood infra + eng).
4) Week 3: production-like soak (48h window) with monitoring dashboards and alerting validation. (owner: Novaworks ops + Redwood SRE).
5) Week 4: readout & go/no-go meeting; handoff checklist for expansion.

Ownership (initial):
- Technical lead (Redwood): Ben Carter — infra, kernels, batch/cache config.
- Product liaison (Redwood): Marissa Cole — success criteria, evaluation design, quality sampling plan.
- Customer product lead: Sanjay Patel — dataset, acceptance sampling, business validators.
- Customer engineering: Leah Kim — integration, traffic shaping for soak.

Key open questions / asks for Novaworks before we kick off:
- Confirm the canonical test set (we attached a manifest; if you have a narrower slice, please flag by Mon 5/31).
- Confirm required security posture for pilot endpoints (VPC or hosted with IP allowlist).
- Any regulatory or data retention constraints we should bake into logs/metrics?

Next steps (action items):
- Sanjay: confirm test set and security posture (due Mon 5/31).
- Ben: prep baseline infra and share temporary API keys (target Wed 6/2).
- Marissa: send the sampling rubric for manual review (target Tue 6/1).

If that slate looks right I’ll turn this into a short mutual action plan and get the SOW draft to you for signature.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: novaworks_kpi_template.xlsx (spreadsheet), test_dataset_manifest.csv (csv)
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novaworks.com>

Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@novaworks.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot KPI slate & ops ownership — Novaworks POC

Thanks Rafael — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Latency: the 350 ms target looks good but we’ll need to confirm median prompt sizes across our top-3 user journeys (I’ll attach a small telemetry dump). Can we set a stretch P95 at 300 ms and a baseline acceptance at 350 ms?
2) Cost: $0.0009/token is acceptable as an initial target; can Redwood provide a modeled run-rate estimate for projected 2M monthly tokens so we can sanity-check our procurement planning?
3) Soak window: 48h sounds right — can we run one soak with representative production traffic shaping (50 RPS steady + 100 RPS short bursts)?

On security: we prefer hosted endpoints behind an IP allowlist for this pilot (no VPC yet). We’ll provide allowed IPs by Monday.

We’ll confirm the test set by EOD Monday. If those clarifications are fine, happy to move forward.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Product, Novaworks
+1 (415) 555-2122

On Fri, May 28, 2027 at 5:05 PM Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novaworks.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rafael — this is very helpful and aligns with our internal expectations. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the kickoff: 
> 
> 1) Latency: the 350 ms target looks good but we’ll need to confirm median prompt sizes across our top-3 user journeys (I’ll attach a small telemetry dump). Can we set a stretch P95 at 300 ms and a baseline acceptance at 350 ms?
> 2) Cost: $0.0009/token is acceptable as an initial target; can Redwood provide a modeled run-rate estimate for projected 2M monthly tokens so we can sanity-check our procurement planning?
> 3) Soak window: 48h sounds right — can we run one soak with representative production traffic shaping (50 RPS steady + 100 RPS short bursts)?

Thanks — yes to all three. Quick answers below and a short follow-up plan: 

- Latency: happy to set a two-tier acceptance — stretch P95 <= 300 ms, baseline P95 <= 350 ms. We’ll include median/95/99 latency buckets in the baseline report.
- Cost modeling: Ben — can you produce a 2M-token/month cost projection with a few config variants (default fp16, q4 quant, and batching profile optimized) and include per-token and per-request breakdown? Target for Wed 6/2.
- Soak: operations can run a 48h soak with the shaping you propose; we’ll validate alerts and failure modes.

Next steps revised: 
- Sanjay: provide telemetry sample + allowed IPs (due Mon 5/31).
- Ben: 2M-token cost projection + infra baseline (due Wed 6/2).
- Marissa: sampling rubric for manual review (due Tue 6/1).
- Rafael: produce MAP & SOW draft once test set confirmed (target Fri 6/4).

I’ll update the attached KPI template with the stretch/baseline columns and send an updated MAP by Monday.

—Rafael
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@novaworks.com>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@novaworks.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 19:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot KPI slate & ops ownership — Novaworks POC

Thanks team — I’ll own the baseline runs and cost modeling. Quick operational notes: 
- I’ll spin up a dedicated pilot pool (no shared capacity) with telemetry enabled and token-level accounting.
- For the cost model, I’ll provide three scenarios (fp16 / q4 / q8) with estimated token throughput and expected latency impact.
- I need the sample telemetry and the manifest to pick the exact slices for the first baseline run. Sanjay — once you drop the sample I’ll schedule the baseline for Wed 6/2 and post the report to the Drive link Rafael shared.

One ask: please confirm whether we should include per-token cache warming (prefix cache) in the baseline or treat that as an optimization for Week 2. I’d recommend treating cache warming as Week 2 so the baseline represents cold-start behavior.

—Ben
